description: The two INTERVAL spellings are DIFFERENT EXPRESSIONS: d + INTERVAL '1' DAY promotes a DATE to a timestamp while d + INTERVAL '1 day' stays a DATE - and anything identifying an expression must keep them apart: two aggregates over the two spellings inside ONE select item render different halves (the canonical-print collision this class exists for), the pair as separate items differs, and the same spelling twice still shares one value. Converted 1:1 from expressions/IntervalSpellingIdentityTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE isp (d DATE, k NUMBER)
CREATE TABLE isp (d DATE, k NUMBER)
SELECT MAX(d + INTERVAL '1' DAY) || '/' || MAX(d + INTERVAL '1 day') AS c FROM isp GROUP BY k
CREATE TABLE isp (d DATE, k NUMBER)
SELECT '<' || MAX(d + INTERVAL '1' DAY) || '>' AS a FROM isp GROUP BY k
SELECT '<' || MAX(d + INTERVAL '1 day') || '>' AS b FROM isp GROUP BY k
CREATE TABLE isp (d DATE, k NUMBER)
SELECT MAX(d + INTERVAL '1 day') || '/' || MAX(d + INTERVAL '1 day') AS c FROM isp GROUP BY k
